title: First job in 1914 with the Black Eagle band across the lake
summary: George recalls his first job on St. Joseph's night 1914 with a small band, naming its members and the two-dollar pay.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: What was your very first job anyway? Did you ever...
My first job was on a St. Joseph's night, 19 to March. 1914 was my first job.
When 19...
And who was that with?
With a little black eagle band. That was across the lake? Across the lake. I left here to go and play.
Do you remember any of the fellows in the band?

One of them was named, the banjo player was named Walter Lewis, and the drum player was named Broussard. And the trumpet player was named, his name was, he had a French name, Val San. I just remember his first name now, but we used to call him Black Eagle, it was real dark. And I think he died just some years ago in...
They called him the... They called him Black Eagle. That's when the band got the name, I don't know.
But he died in the Tantry, I think, just some years back, he killed a man out there in McCormick, Mississippi.

And he was a trombone player in the band. Yeah, there was a trombone player in the band. And then that was Earl Foster's brother. I think he was with us right now. Earl Foster's brother. I don't know.
He quit playing a long time. And let's see, you had drums, bass, trombone trumpet? Mm-hm.
They had drums, bass, trombone, trumpet?

They had a fellow by the name of Manuel, he was playing bass. The drum player was a people named Bruce Aldo, Burrow, Roosevelt Burrow was a drummer. He had goat hires on the drum, we had that on the goat hires because they couldn't get the hair and the goat hires for the drum.
Did you get paid you say?
Two dollars.
Two dollars in those days? How long would you have to work?
About four in the morning.
You started what time?
Yeah.
Eight to four. Dude, all that's pretty good to pay, wasn't it?
Eight dollars. Yeah, it was a lot of fun out there. A lot of fun.
